summary:
R4 is the story of the model right now — 40-14 (74%) on trends and a perfect 20-5 (+17.0u) strong-play record across every window because it simply hasn't had time to cool off (n=25-54 across the board). That small sample means treat its edges as directional, not gospel, but it lines up with every other rating on 9 of today's 10 games, so where it agrees, lean in. Meanwhile R1 and R2's sp category is riding 5-game winning streaks with a jump from 52-53% season to 53% over the last 14 — modest, but combined with the trends category running hot everywhere (58% at n=188 for R1/R2/R3 vs low-50s season baseline), trends+sp is your best category pairing at 56.9% (231-175, n=406) historically.

Today's board leans one direction: full four-rating consensus on WSN (all four rate them +1.95 to +2.55 over COL, the widest gap on the slate), and stacked consensus fades on TBR@DET, PHI@SEA, CHC@ARI and CLE@LAA all in the -1.0 to -2.0 range. The only split ticket is PIT@SDP, where R1-R3 lean PIT by a hair (-0.14 to -0.28) but R4 flips to SDP (+0.37) — with R4's current form, I'd give SDP the tiebreak there. TBR@DET is worth flagging on team trends: TBR is 25-12 (68%) when picked this season and 18-5 (78%, +22.0u) on strong plays, one of the model's best teams-when-liked, and today's rating gap (-1.93 to -2.04) qualifies as a strong-play spread. Similarly, BOS is 32-9 (78%, n=41) when picked and 17-5 (77%, +16.0u) strong, but today's BOS@MIA delta is thin (-0.03 to -0.37) — good team history, weak signal, treat as a lean not a strong play. Avoid leaning on bullpen_fatigue anywhere today; it's cold across all three main ratings (45% at n=188, down from 47% season) and none of today's deltas are driven by it.
